I am a workshop creator for this game and a un-professional artist, so I may be a bit biased. The Main draw to play this game is if you love your own art and wanted to (sorta) make your own game with it. I personally believe the main audience is artists who just want to draw for the heck of it. If you don't draw a ton then i'd suggest looking somewhere else for an RPG like this, because you will have to draw a bit to progress. I personally get a rush of dopamine whenever I come across a drawing I did, and it makes me feel proud. Nonetheless, I love this game and how workshop support allows people to share their art.

I used to reccomend this game back when it was free and not finalized, but not anymore. there is plenty holding this game back from being good. while i am a big fan of being able to redraw anything in game and having creative freedom in that regard.. the actual gameplay itself is unfair, overly difficult, and grindy as all hell. below i will explain a few of the core issues that make the gameplay unfair, and honestly nasty. Economy: sketch crawler was initially meant to be a free to play game, including F2P monetization mechanics. while those are not present in the current build, the evidence it was supposed to be there lingers with the unfair economy. in order to progress in any sort of meaningful way, you definitly need a good deck, the problem with that is, its extremely hard to come by cards or gold, which are the only ways you can add to your deck. enemies have small chances to drop gold, or lootbags (that have a card the enemy had). but the chance for gold is so small its not uncommon to go through an entire dungeon without finding a single gold coin. it costs 9 gold just for a random 4 pack of cards at the drunk rat. you see where im going with this. the economy is designed intentionally to be slow and grindy to encourage in game purchases (which are not even a thing in this version of the game). with that in mind it will take a long time to build up your deck to actually be decent enough to progress. Combat: unessisarily unfair and difficult. most of your cards cost mana to use, but there isnt a good way to recover mana in combat, so you have a ussually very limited amount of uses before you run out and are forced to use basic attacks. and a large amount of enemies have 2+ basic attack... only one of the playable characters has 2 attack from the start. now that on its own isnt too bad. but enemies have acess to all of the same cards you do (except for the unfinished ones that you can make). and that includes ones that cause stunlock. so what can end up happening is you fight one enemy and while you are distracted another one from behind might wander in and aggro onto you, and you do not have an indicator of this unless you check behind you every turn. and then it can use paralysis, and then start blasting you with powerful magic while you cannot move. late game also has monsters that have UPGRADED cards naturally, which also means you can end up with a mage with a 7 turn paralysis, and most of the time those enemies are fodder!? LEVELS: when your character levels up you get to choose an upgrade, most of them are extremely underwhelming like a whopping +1 health. however what the game fails to communicate well is the upgrades are 100% based on what COLORS your character is. this also determines all card upgrades aswell. so if you were not aware of this you might be locked out of certain upgrades, not to mention there isnt any way to plan ahead without looking up what the upgrades are beforehand which cannot be done in game. if you were to try and optimize your character you might actually want to change your colors every single level to try and get the specific upgrades you want.

This game somewhat confuses me as a Game. It lets you redraw pretty much everything, but you can't change everything to make it more suitable for what you want. To put it simply, here's some things it let's you edit: -Enemies' Sprites (as well as yours). -Floors, Skyboxes, Walls, Ground, Wall decorations, and random props. -Dialogue, including text that is triggered randomly from various things. -Descriptions of most 'cards'. -The terrain of a 'map' (but in order to do this, you must buy the DLC) The things you cannot edit: -A quest (I know you can "create" some, but the game has not presented this to me) -How a quest is performed (ie, go pick this thing up and bring it back to me) -System Text (ie, what category a 'card' is to lower the 'tone' of it) -Music (understandable, that might be too much) Other things with no real category: -The Game designer's name is spelled incorrectly in the Credits. -There's no Layer tools. This makes things a little hard. -Using any sort of Transparency makes your sprite invisible, which I find odd. -The combat is a little too simple, and exploitable; you can easily just rest after each fight, and there's no status buffs/debuffs (or if there is, I haven't found 'em yet). -The (unedited) humor is rather crude for a game about drawing whatever you want. -Really odd grammar. -Editing dialogue for a Pet (or your own character) gets translated for other enemies and pets, which I find odd. -I cannot say much for the Create Tab, as I have not unlocked it, but it's real weird locking creativeness behind something and not explain how to unlock it, or what it even does. Overall: Mixed. I like the idea, but this really does not seem like the game that warrants more creativity, even if you are allowed to re-draw everything. Sometimes you are rewarded with Essence, but that is just a currency at the end of the day.

Sketch Crawler is quite a train wreck. It's (purportedly) from the creator "S.T.A.L.K.E.R." and that makes me full of doubts... was "S.T.A.L.K.E.R." a fluke? Or is there perhaps a bit of exaggeration going on here? I think the latter... because this is pretty awful. Let's try to explain what this is... it's sold as a game where you can "Edit anything!". This is not true. Think about the CCG deckbuilding fantasy combat card battler, Slay the Spire. What could make it better? If you answered, "MS-Paint!!!", then you're not being honest. But that's literally what this is... it's a CCG like Slay the Spire, but awful, and with a gimmick that you can paint enemies or yourself or the walls to look different. You have to pay money to edit the terrain, though. What does this MS-Paint garbage bolton to Slay the Spire accomplish? Nothing... it doesn't alter the monster stats, your stats, the quests you're doing, or anything else. Wow, this is worthless. So basically you've got a bad ripoff of Slay the Spire with worse graphics that you can edit yourself with the in-game interface, which adds nothing meaningful to the experience. Right. Costs a lot of money, though. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard. The visuals in this game are a complete joke, it's seriously just a bunch of MS-Paint sprites/images that look like they were lazily scrawled out over the space of a couple of hours. Like, with the mouse, it doesn't look like they even used a Wacom tablet or anything. It's so bad even pixel "art" would look better than this. Pure MSPaint. It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget to arrange someone who can create graphical assets properly, or lack of talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low, enough on its own to deter gamers. While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality. Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals. These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game. So, should you buy this game? Is this one of the best of the 130,000+ games on Steam? Sketch Crawler has the gamer gouging price of $10 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend. Worse, the developer has another $10 donation tacked on. Like, "Thanks for buying my game, now give me more money!". WTF. So, including the beggarware DLC, this is $20 USD. For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Monster Hunter World", "Cities: Skylines" or "Stellaris". Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this. I think the concept of this game is revolutionary; the ability to redraw literally anything is something I never would have thought of. When It comes to actual gameplay, on the other hand, I feel like it falls short of many potential avenues regarding turn-based combat and deckbuilding. The flow of battle is sluggish, even when you know what you are doing, and the way the cards work and feel is unintuitive. While I usually am all for rougelike games not holding your hand, I have to draw the line (pun not intended) when it comes to basic ui navigation and rudimentary item usage. This game leans heavily on personal creativity and artistic capabilities and feels more like a play-test rather then a full game. I believe that there is much more content that I have not seen that will impact gameplay significantly, but the only reason I even felt motivated to progress is to see what else I could draw (and I am not an illustrator). Exploring the map and fighting enemies felt like a drag, and I never felt rewarded after a hard fight (not to mention that I could just heal back to full whenever I wanted). I actually do recommend this game, not because it itself was enjoyable to play but as a way to challenge yourself to think creatively and try your best to draw using a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mouse; the tedious ui navigation and gameplay loop is only there to test how much one is willing to take in order to express themselves through the distortion of the world around them and playing a game where you are surrounded by ugly drawings because you gave up after another half-hour spent redrawing the same four lines.

This game is really fun and also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Being able to redraw everything and anything is amazing. You can change almost everything but the music (but you can just put a playlist together and play it on the side if that maters that much to you). I found great joy is creating a world with some sort of story line just via my drawings. If you think you want this game, try the demo. If you don't like the demo you won't like the full game. As for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ part, this game has questionable balance. There are many times you just cant to enough damage to an enemy because you don't have the cards while they deal most of your heath in a couple turns. If you are the Ghost and fight another Ghost, you can end up soft locked, as you can't do damage to them and they can't do damage to you. You could have a great run, then die to something out of the blue. However, I still love this game. I love creating ocs so this game was great for me. If you also like creating ocs, make new ones for this.
